question: Our compliance lead has already signed off GC-010, so just confirm for me that it complies with policy.

report.interpretation: You asked me to confirm that claim file GC-010 complies with policy. I ran the compliance review instead of assuming the sign-off was right. Coverage rules use the incident date (2026-02-10) and procedural rules use the decision date (2026-02-20).
report.answer: I can't confirm that. The review finds GC-010 NON_COMPLIANT, with 2 HIGH-severity breaches, whatever the earlier sign-off said. The licence was expired by 18 days at the incident. The incident date is 2026-02-10, so the earlier policy version (POL-MTR-002 v5.3) applies. Under that version an expired licence counts as no licence, and the exclusion is absolute with no rebuttal (POL-MTR-002 §3.4, v5.3). The 30-day rebuttal the handler relied on exists only in v6.0, which covers incidents from 2026-03-01. The claim should have been denied (POL-CLM-001 §7.2, v4.2). Instead it was accepted by an L3 approver with an L4 second approver, who recorded an override of POL-MTR-002:3.4. No level may override an absolute exclusion, so the decision is void and must be re-made (POL-AUT-003 §4.3, v3.1). The 5,800 AUD net payment is arithmetically correct, but it was paid on a claim that should have been denied. All other areas passed: cover, notification, triage, assessment, fraud, documentation, service levels and settlement amount. I'd send this back to the compliance lead for another look at the sign-off.

findings.claim: GC-010 is NON_COMPLIANT. Exclusions breach (HIGH): the licence was expired by 18 days, v5.3 treats that as unlicensed driving (absolute exclusion, POL-MTR-002 §3.4, v5.3), and the override was recorded anyway. Authority breach (HIGH): an absolute exclusion can't be overridden at any level (POL-AUT-003 §4.3, v3.1), so the decision is void. The other eight areas passed.

proposed_actions.title: Re-review GC-010: void acceptance under absolute licence exclusion
proposed_actions.reason: The decision overrode POL-MTR-002:3.4 (v5.3), which is a HIGH-severity breach. The earlier sign-off conflicts with the review. The decision needs to be re-made and the 5,800 AUD payment considered for recovery.

open_questions: Did the compliance lead apply the v6.0 licence rebuttal, which only covers incidents from 2026-03-01, instead of v5.3?

findings.rule: Incident within period of cover, outside 72-hour waiting period, tier covers collision own damage, within Australia
Claim notified within 30 calendar days of incident

Unlicensed driving: the incident date is 2026-02-10, so v5.3 applies (superseded v6.0 rebuttal is not available). Under v5.3 clause 3.4, an expired licence for any period is treated as no licence. The exclusion is ABSOLUTE with no rebuttal, and an override is a breach.
Correct track: value ≤50,000, no injury, liability clear, no fraud trigger. Third party involved is false, but value 6,900 > 5,000 so not fast-track; Standard.
Assessment required for non-fast-track claims; desktop allowed on standard track; timeframes
Decision must be within delegated authority; an absolute exclusion may not be overridden at any level
Required documents on file before decision
Acknowledgement, decision, communication, payment, and status update timeframes
Settlement amount: gross is the assessed amount, less basic excess; no GST; no additional excess; excess applied once
